title: dns command supports only A/AAAA/PTR via the OS resolver — no TXT/MX/CNAME/SRV and no custom server
existing_state: DnsCommand whitelists exactly A, AAAA, and PTR (Services/Scripting/Commands/DnsCommand.cs:118-123) and resolves through System.Net.Dns (`GetHostAddressesAsync`/`GetHostEntryAsync`, DnsCommand.cs:143-154), which can only use the machine's configured resolver. The allowed-key table is `host, type, timeout, into, on_error` (Services/Scripting/ScriptParser.cs:131) — no `server:` key. For a network-operations tool this rules out the two most common verification tasks: checking TXT/MX/CNAME/SRV/NS records, and asking a SPECIFIC DNS server (e.g., 'has the record change propagated to each site's resolver?'). Any unsupported type fails the step with 'Dns type ... is not supported' (DnsCommand.cs:45-48).
recommendation: Swap the System.Net.Dns backend behind the existing IDnsResolver seam (DnsCommand.cs:137-141) for a real DNS client (the DnsClient NuGet package is the standard choice) and extend IsSupportedType to TXT/MX/CNAME/SRV/NS/SOA. Add an optional `server:` option (IP or host of the resolver to query, defaulting to system resolvers) to DnsOptions and the parser key table at ScriptParser.cs:131. Keep the existing capture shape (`into` list + `into_count`) and render MX/SRV records as 'priority host' strings for backward-compatible list handling.
user_benefit: DNS verification scripts (propagation checks across site resolvers, MX/TXT audits before mail or ACME changes) can run inside SSH_Helper presets instead of pushing engineers back out to nslookup/dig in a separate terminal.

evidence.note: type whitelist: A, AAAA, PTR only
SystemDnsResolver wraps System.Net.Dns — system resolver only, no server selection
no server key in the dns option set
